subject: Hosted API: token stacking & onboarding pricing for two new products
messages:
From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@tidalapps.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for two new product lines + multi-team billing question

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from the product team: we are planning to launch two new products in Q4 that will both call Redwood's hosted API. High level projections:
- Product A (consumer chat): ~200M tokens/month in steady state by month 3
- Product B (search/rerank + short replies): ~60M tokens/month

We expect a soft pilot in September (small volume), then ramp to the numbers above over ~8 weeks. We want to understand:
1) How you handle multi-product / multi-team billing under a single account — can committed credits be shared or stacked across products?
2) Example per-token price tiers for monthly volumes (we're trying to map to our internal cost model)
3) Any guidance on burst capacity and short-term top-ups for launch spikes

I attached our expected usage export (TidalApps_expected_usage_Q3.csv). Can you propose a pricing path that gets us to a reasonable blended rate once both products are live? Procurement will want a 12-month commit example if it helps.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Walker
Head of Platform, TidalApps
sam.walker@tidalapps.com

Attachment: TidalApps_expected_usage_Q3.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@tidalapps.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for two new product lines + multi-team billing question

Hi Sam — thanks for the file and the clarity on ramp. Short answers up front: yes, committed credits can be consolidated across products under one contract (we call that "stacking" for multi-team accounts), and we can model burst/top-up buckets for launch spikes.

Below is a concrete starting proposal (pilot -> commit path) you can review with procurement:
- Pilot (1–3 months): pay-as-you-go hosted rates, with a one-time launch credit of $10k applied to the first invoice.
- 12-month committed plan (example blended math):
  - Committed monthly spend: $150,000/month (12-month term = $1.8M)
  - Expected monthly tokens (blended): 260M tokens/month (Product A + B)
  - Blended effective rate: $150,000 / 260M = ~$0.000577 per token
  - Tier structure we use for pricing guidance (hosted API):
    * 0–50M: $0.0009/token
    * 50M–200M: $0.0006/token
    * 200M+: $0.00045/token
  - With a 12-month commit and stacking, your blended ends up near the ~$0.00057 range (illustrative).

Operational notes:
- Credits are shared at the org level; you can map products to sub-accounts for reporting.
- Burst capacity: we provide a short-term burst bucket (pay-as-you-go overage) and can add a paid burst reserve for predictable launches.
- Rollover: unused committed credits do not automatically roll beyond the monthly period unless explicitly negotiated (we can include a limited rollover window in the SOW).

Next steps I suggest:
1) If procurement is ok with an illustrative $150k/mo example, we draft an SOW with a 30-day pilot -> 12-month commit path and define a launch burst bucket.
2) Monica (CC) can confirm operational readiness and SLO language.

I'll put together a formal SOW template and a clean pricing spreadsheet for procurement. Does that direction work?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks Karthik — that helps a lot. A couple clarifying items from procurement and platform:
- The $150k/mo baseline is within range, but procurement will push for a blended closer to $0.0005/token if we can justify it for a 12-month commitment.
- We need a mechanism for short-term credit top-ups that show as "reserved burst" on the invoice (procurement likes this for predictable spend).
- Important: our teams want per-product reporting so engineers can track token consumption by product/feature. Can reporting be sub-accounted and visible in the console?

I've attached a cleaned usage export with expected week-by-week ramp (TidalApps_expected_usage_Q3.csv). We can also share an internal SLA checklist if you want Monica to start review.

If you can send a redlineable SOW and a sample invoice showing the blended math + burst reserve line item, procurement will likely fast-track.

—Sam

- Margin check: lauren — is the above within acceptable discounting guidelines?
- Ops: monica — can we promise sub-account reporting and include a 3-month limited rollover on unused committed credits in the SOW? Also need your SRE note on burst handling and latency SLOs for high QPS events.

If we can do that, I'll prepare the SOW and a sample invoice with a separate line item: "Launch burst reserve (prepaid)".

-Karthik

Hi Sam — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise offer and a sample invoice to share with procurement. Key points:

Proposal summary (finalizable in SOW):
- Term: 12 months
- Committed monthly spend: $150,000/month (12 months = $1.8M)
- Prepaid launch burst reserve: $120,000 (applied to Q4 overages)
- Reporting: sub-account token reporting per product in the Console (daily granularity)
- Credit stacking: committed credits apply at the org level across Product A & Product B
- Rollover: up to 3 months of unused committed credits can be rolled forward (capped at 25% of monthly committed volume)
- Operational SLOs: standard Hosted API SLOs apply; Monica will attach a short ops addendum with latency targets and recommended concurrency limits for launches.

Blended math (illustrative):
- Expected monthly tokens: 260M
- Monthly committed spend: $150k + (launch reserve amortized for first 3 months = $40k) => effective spend month 1–3 = $190k; months 4–12 = $150k
- Approx blended effective rate, year one (amortized): ~$0.00051 / token

Attachments included: RDW_SOW_template_v2.pdf (redlineable), sample_invoice_tidalapps_Q4.pdf, TidalApps_SOW_draft.pdf (your editable draft).
